# Character — Ironclad

**Character:** Ironclad

**Color:** Red

## Identity

The Ironclad is an aggressive, front-line warrior who excels at Strength scaling, Exhaust synergies, and self-sustain through HP recovery. The Ironclad's playstyle rewards aggressive play — killing enemies fast and healing the damage taken. The Ironclad punishes enemies who don't die quickly and has the tools to scale damage to absurd heights.

**Playstyle:** Aggressive with built-in sustain. The Ironclad wants to hit hard, scale Strength, and use exhaust mechanics to thin the deck and trigger powerful synergies. The starting relic (Burning Blood) encourages taking fights because you heal after every combat.

### Strengths

- Best Strength scaling in the game — can reach very high damage numbers
- Strong exhaust synergies that simultaneously thin the deck and generate value
- Built-in sustain through Burning Blood and HP-recovery cards
- Excellent frontloaded damage — can end hallway fights quickly
- Access to Barricade for infinite block retention

### Weaknesses

- Block cards are generally weaker than Silent or Defect — relies on killing fast rather than blocking forever
- Exhaust strategies can run out of cards if not managed carefully
- Vulnerable to fights that punish aggression (enemies that punish attacking, or scale faster than you)
- Some key cards are expensive (2-3 cost) requiring energy management

## Starting Relic

**Name:** Burning Blood

**Effect:** Heal 6 HP at the end of combat

**Strategic Value:** Enables aggressive play. The 6 HP healing means you can take more damage in fights and still be healthy for the next fight. This encourages fighting more enemies and hunting elites.

### Tips

- Burning Blood makes upgrading at campfires more attractive — you have passive healing already
- The 6 HP adds up: over 15 fights in an act, that's 90 HP healed passively
- Don't rely on it exclusively — it won't save you from big hits
- It's most valuable in Act 1 where individual fight damage tends to be lower

## Archetypes

### Strength Scaling

The quintessential Ironclad strategy. Stack Strength through permanent buffs and turn every attack into a devastating blow. Multi-hit attacks become especially powerful with Strength.

#### Core Cards

- Demon Form — gain 2/3 Strength per turn. The best Strength scaling card. Once online, every turn you get stronger.
- Inflame — gain 2/3 Strength permanently. Simple, effective, no setup required.
- Spot Weakness — gain 3/4 Strength if enemy intends to attack. Conditional but very efficient.
- Limit Break — double your Strength. Insane with any Strength source. Upgraded, it doesn't exhaust.
- Heavy Blade — deals 14 damage, affected by Strength 3x/5x. The payoff card for Strength builds.

#### Support Cards

- Pummel — multi-hit attack, each hit benefits from Strength
- Sword Boomerang — hits 3/4 random enemies, each hit gets Strength bonus
- Twin Strike — hits twice, double Strength benefit
- Headbutt — damage + puts card on top of draw pile (get Limit Break back quickly)

#### Strengths

- Damage scales infinitely — each turn your attacks hit harder
- Multi-hit attacks amplify Strength enormously
- Simple to pilot — play Strength cards, then play attacks
- Works with almost any attack card in your deck

#### Weaknesses

- Slow to start — Demon Form costs 3 energy and takes turns to build up
- Needs block cards to survive while Strength ramps up
- Vulnerable to Artifact enemies who can prevent debuffs that support Strength strategies

#### Key Relic Synergies

- Vajra — +1 Strength at combat start. Free scaling on every fight.
- Girya — Lift at campfires for +1 Strength permanently. Long-term investment.
- Red Skull — +3 Strength when below 50% HP. Risky but powerful.

### Exhaust Engine

Build a deck around exhausting cards to trigger powerful synergies. Dark Embrace draws cards, Feel No Pain generates block, Dead Branch creates free cards. The exhaust engine can thin your deck to just your best cards while generating massive value.

#### Core Cards

- Corruption — ALL Skills cost 0 but exhaust after play. The centerpiece of exhaust strategies. With Feel No Pain, every skill you play generates block AND draws cards.
- Dark Embrace — whenever a card is exhausted, draw 1 card. Turns exhaust into card advantage.
- Feel No Pain — whenever a card is exhausted, gain 3/4 block. Turns exhaust into defense.
- Sentinel — gain 5/8 block. When exhausted, gain 2/3 energy. Extra energy fuels big turns.
- Second Wind — exhaust ALL non-attack cards in hand, gain 5/7 block per card exhausted. Massive block burst.

#### Support Cards

- Fiend Fire — exhaust your entire hand, deal 7 damage per card exhausted. Finisher card.
- Burning Pact — exhaust 1 card, draw 2/3 cards. Fuel for the engine.
- True Grit — gain 7/9 block, exhaust a card. Block + exhaust trigger.
- Offering — lose 6 HP, gain 2 energy, draw 3/5 cards. Powerful cycle card.
- Havoc — play the top card of draw pile for free, exhaust it. Free value.

#### Strengths

- Self-thinning deck — as you exhaust cards, remaining draws become more consistent
- Massive card advantage with Dark Embrace
- Enormous block generation with Feel No Pain + Corruption
- Can generate more value per turn than almost any other strategy
- Dead Branch makes the engine self-sustaining by replacing exhausted cards

#### Weaknesses

- Requires specific pieces to function — Corruption without Feel No Pain can leave you defenseless
- Can exhaust too many cards and run out of options if engine isn't fully assembled
- Expensive to set up — Corruption costs 3, Dark Embrace costs 2
- Fights that are too short don't give the engine time to start

#### Key Relic Synergies

- Dead Branch — create a random card whenever you exhaust a card. The dream relic for exhaust builds.
- Charon's Ashes — deal 3 damage to ALL enemies whenever you exhaust a card. Free AOE.
- Strange Spoon — 50% chance exhausted cards go to discard instead. Reusable engine pieces.

### Block Engine

A defensive Ironclad build centered around Barricade (block doesn't expire between turns) and Body Slam (deal damage equal to your block). Build up massive block over multiple turns, then one-shot enemies with Body Slam.

#### Core Cards

- Barricade — your block persists between turns. The key enabler — without Barricade, block resets each turn.
- Body Slam — deal damage equal to your current block. 0 cost. The payoff for accumulating block.
- Shrug It Off — gain 8/11 block, draw 1 card. The best Ironclad block card — block + draw.
- Metallicize — gain 3/4 block at end of every turn permanently. Free block that stacks with Barricade.
- Entrench — double your current block. With Barricade, this gets insane quickly.

#### Support Cards

- Impervious — gain 30/40 block. Huge single-turn block gain.
- Flame Barrier — gain 12/16 block, deal 4 damage when attacked. Block + damage.
- Iron Wave — gain 5/7 block and deal 5/7 damage. Versatile but unexciting.
- Power Through — gain 15/20 block but add Wounds to hand. Big block but clutters hand.

#### Strengths

- Nearly invincible once Barricade is online — block accumulates faster than enemies can damage you
- Body Slam provides scaling damage without any attack cards — your block IS your damage
- Very safe and consistent once set up
- Entrench doubles block exponentially — goes from 30 to 60 to 120 to 240...

#### Weaknesses

- Barricade costs 3 energy — slow to get online
- Without Barricade, the entire strategy falls apart
- Vulnerable to enemies that remove block or bypass it
- Slow to kill — Block/Body Slam builds take many turns to win

## Act By Act Plan

### Act1

#### Priorities

- Get frontloaded damage to kill hallway enemies in 2-3 turns (Carnage, Pommel Strike, Headbutt)
- Find at least one scaling source (Inflame, Demon Form, or Spot Weakness)
- Pick up 1-2 block cards beyond starting Defends (Shrug It Off is premium)
- Upgrade Bash to Bash+ (3 Vulnerable is a massive damage increase)
- Remove 1-2 Strikes at shops

**Card Priorities:** Attacks > Scaling > Block. You need to kill things before you need to block.

**Elite Readiness:** Fight your first elite after picking up 2-3 good cards. Bash+ plus a strong attack is usually enough.

**Boss Preparation:** Ensure you have some scaling (even just Inflame) and enough block to survive 5-6 turns.

### Act2

#### Priorities

- Solidify your deck's identity — Strength scaling, Exhaust engine, or Block/Body Slam
- Add key Power cards (Demon Form, Corruption, Barricade) if offered
- Improve block density to handle Act 2's harder enemies
- Remove remaining Strikes and Defends
- Upgrade key cards aggressively

**Card Priorities:** Scaling > Block > Draw. Your deck should have its core strategy by end of Act 2.

**Elite Readiness:** Your deck should handle elites comfortably if your strategy is coming together.

**Boss Preparation:** Ensure your scaling is online and reliable. Act 2 bosses are significantly harder than Act 1.

### Act3

#### Priorities

- Skip most card rewards — your deck is built
- Upgrade remaining key cards at campfires
- Remove any remaining filler cards at shops
- Ensure your deck can handle the Act 3 boss specifically
- Conserve HP for the final boss fight

**Card Priorities:** Only take cards that directly address a weakness against the final boss.

**Focus:** Optimization, not addition. Make your existing cards better, don't add new ones.

## Common Pitfalls

**Too Many Powers:** Don't take every Power card. Powers cost energy to play and don't help you survive the turn you play them. 3-4 Powers is usually enough.

**No Frontload:** Demon Form is amazing but does nothing on the turn you play it. Make sure you have attacks that deal immediate damage.

**Ignoring Block:** Ironclad has the best attacks but mediocre block. Don't neglect defense — Shrug It Off, Impervious, and True Grit are important.

**Exhaust Without Payoff:** Taking Corruption without Feel No Pain or Dark Embrace leaves you without skills to play. Don't start exhausting until you have the payoff pieces.

**Overreliance On Burning Blood:** 6 HP per fight is nice but won't save you from 30+ damage elite fights. Don't take extra damage just because you have healing.

**Heavy Blade Without Strength:** Heavy Blade is mediocre without Strength. It only becomes powerful with 5+ Strength stacks.

## Advanced Synergies And Reworks

Grandmaster-level Ironclad knowledge: cards reworked in STS2, current top combos, and anti-pattern warnings.

### Stoke The Dead Branch Card

**Card:** Stoke

**Rework:** Exhausts your ENTIRE hand and replaces every card with a random Ironclad card (upgraded versions if Stoke itself is upgraded). Stoke does NOT exhaust itself.

**Why Top Tier:** Functions like the Dead Branch relic baked into a card. Pair with Feel No Pain and Dark Embrace and you generate massive block/draw every time you play it. Self-recurring because Stoke doesn't exhaust.

#### Best Partners

- Feel No Pain
- Dark Embrace
- Corruption
- Second Wind

### Perfected Strike Exhaust Safety

**Card:** Perfected Strike

**Rework:** Now counts Strike cards in your EXHAUST pile, not just your deck.

**Implication:** You can safely exhaust your starter Strikes (via Corruption, True Grit, Headbutt, etc.) WITHOUT losing your late-game Perfected Strike damage scaling. This was the main weakness of Perfected Strike builds in STS1.

**Build Pattern:** Take Perfected Strike + heavy exhaust → exhaust all 5 starter Strikes through combat → Perfected Strike now hits for huge numbers AND your deck is thin

### Pillage Hellraiser Perfected Strike Combo

#### Cards

- Pillage
- Hellraiser
- Perfected Strike

**The Combo:** Hellraiser auto-plays any Strike card the moment it's drawn. Pillage draws cards until you hit a non-attack. If you thin your deck of skills/powers, Pillage will draw your entire deck of Perfected Strikes and auto-play all of them via Hellraiser.

**Result:** Game-ending damage in a single play, particularly devastating against single-target bosses

#### Deck Requirements

- Thin skills/powers
- Multiple Perfected Strikes
- Hellraiser power online
- Pillage in hand

### Dominate Strength Scaling

**Card:** Dominate

**Rework:** Now scales your Strength directly based on the enemy's Vulnerable stacks

**Implication:** Dominate is now the premier Strength-generation tool for Ironclad. Pair with Vulnerable-application cards (Bash, Sword Boomerang, Inflame) to ramp Strength faster than any other character

**Synergy:** Bash applies 2 Vulnerable → Dominate grants +2 Strength. Bash+ + Dominate stacks Strength at a brutal rate.

### Cruelty Vulnerable Amplifier

**Card:** Cruelty

**Effect:** Massively multiplies damage dealt to Vulnerable enemies

**Build Pattern:** Vulnerable application + Cruelty + raw attacks = boss-killer combo. Especially strong vs single-target Act 3 bosses.

### Defensive Anchors

#### Colossus

**Effect:** 50% damage reduction from Vulnerable enemies

**Tier:** S-tier defensive monolith

**Synergy:** Compounds with all your Vulnerable application — every Bash, Sword Boomerang, etc. doubles your effective HP for that fight

#### Unmovable

**Effect:** Doubles the FIRST block gained each turn

**Tier:** S-tier defensive monolith

**Best With:** Single big-block cards (Iron Wave, Shrug It Off) rather than many small blocks. Order block cards so the biggest hits first.

### Infinite Loops Are Dead

STS2 deliberately broke most easy Ironclad infinites. Don't try to build the old STS1 loops.

#### Broken Loops

- Expect a Fight — now explicitly prevents gaining additional energy on the turn it's played. No more 0-cost energy infinites.
- Bloodletting — rebalanced to prevent loop exploits
- Spite — reworked: now hits multiple times if you LOSE HP, not draws cards (no more draw-loop spite)
- Forgotten Ritual — exhausts after a single use, no more Power-loop

**What To Build Instead:** Big-card decks with Stoke + exhaust payoffs, Perfected Strike + exhaust scaling, or Demon Form + Limit Break Strength scaling. Quality over quantity.

### Aeonglass Counter Archetype

Aeonglass (Act 3 boss as of patch 0.105.0, replaced the removed Doormaker) adds a Wither status to your hand every 4 non-status cards played. Ironclad's BIG-CARD decks naturally play few cards per turn, making them a strong counter.

#### Build For Aeonglass

- Bludgeon, Demon Form, Reaper, Heavy Blade as your core damage — fewer plays per turn
- Stoke recursion is RISKY here — Stoke replaces your hand with random Ironclad cards which can include many cantrips; count those plays against the Wither threshold
- Avoid cycle-heavy Pillage+Hellraiser combos here — they auto-play many cards and rapidly generate Withers
- If Withers stack: 1 energy to play and clear, or 2 damage at end of turn — usually cheaper to play them through during a turn you have spare energy

**Ironclad Specific Play:** Demon Form + 2-cost big attacks turns the fight into a strength-scaling race. Generate 30+ damage per turn from 2-3 cards, end the fight before Wither pollution becomes lethal.
